title: Monotone constraints on LightGBM for polarity and size descriptors
spec: In fit_predict, build the LGBMRegressor with monotone_constraints set per feature. Look up the column index of each of these RDKit descriptor names in Descriptors.descList: TPSA (-1), NumHDonors (-1), NumHAcceptors (-1), MolWt (-1), MolLogP (+1). Leave all other features unconstrained (0). Build the vector with the same length as the featurized matrix, using the names from Descriptors.descList in order, and pass it as monotone_constraints with monotone_constraints_method='advanced'. Keep every other hyperparameter, the SVR blend and the 50/50 weights unchanged. The goal is to restrict the trees to physically plausible directions so they generalize across unseen scaffolds.

title: LightGBM with linear leaves
spec: Replace the LightGBM member's constant leaves with linear models by setting linear_tree=True, linear_lambda=1.0 on the LGBMRegressor, keeping n_estimators=500, learning_rate=0.03, num_leaves=15 and the other settings. Before fitting, replace NaN and inf in the descriptor matrix by 0 as now and clip to a finite range so the leaf regressions stay stable. Keep the SVR member and the 50/50 blend exactly as they are. Only the tree structure of the LightGBM member changes.

title: Inverse-density sample weights from scaffold cluster size
spec: Compute the Murcko scaffold (rdkit.Chem.Scaffolds.MurckoScaffold.MurckoScaffoldSmiles) for each training molecule. Count how many training molecules share each scaffold and set sample weight w_i = 1/sqrt(count_i), then normalize the weights to mean 1. Pass these weights as sample_weight to LGBMRegressor.fit and to SVR.fit (SVR accepts sample_weight). This stops large scaffold families from dominating the fit, which matters because the test folds are split by scaffold. Keep all other hyperparameters and the 50/50 blend unchanged.

title: Learning-rate decay schedule for the LightGBM member
spec: Keep the LightGBM member's structure (500 trees, num_leaves=15, subsample=0.8, colsample_bytree=0.5, min_child_samples=10), but train it with a decaying learning rate. Pass callbacks=[lightgbm.reset_parameter(learning_rate=lambda it: 0.05 * (0.1 ** (it / 500)))] to fit, with the base learning_rate set to 0.05 so the rate falls from 0.05 to about 0.005 over the run. Import lightgbm.reset_parameter. Leave the SVR member and the 50/50 blend unchanged. The aim is a smoother late-stage fit with the same number of trees.

title: Inner-holdout early stopping to choose LightGBM tree count
spec: Inside fit_predict, split the training set once, with a seed-based shuffle, into 85% fit and 15% validation. Fit the LGBMRegressor on the 85% part with n_estimators=2000, learning_rate=0.03 and eval_set on the 15% part with eval_metric='l1'. Use callbacks=[lightgbm.early_stopping(100, verbose=False)] to find best_iteration. Then refit the LightGBM model on all training data with n_estimators set to round(1.1 * best_iteration). Keep the SVR member and the 50/50 blend unchanged. This replaces the fixed 500-tree count with a data-driven one.

title: LightGBM leaf embeddings as input to an RBF SVR
spec: After fitting the LightGBM member (unchanged hyperparameters), call model.predict(X, pred_leaf=True) on the training and test descriptor matrices to get leaf indices per tree. One-hot encode the leaf indices with sklearn OneHotEncoder(handle_unknown='ignore') fitted on the training part. Fit an SVR (kernel='rbf', C=3, epsilon=0.1, gamma='scale') on these sparse leaf-indicator features, with the training targets y. Use the SVR prediction as the second blend member in place of the current descriptor SVR, keeping the 50/50 weights. The leaves act as learned, target-aware descriptor bins that the kernel can smooth over.

title: Shrink blended predictions toward the training median
spec: After computing the blend 0.5*p_lgb + 0.5*p_svr, shrink the predictions toward the training median: final = med + s*(blend - med), where med = np.median(y) and s = 0.9. Apply the shrinkage only inside fit_predict on the returned array. Keep all models and their hyperparameters unchanged. The shrinkage is meant to reduce variance on unseen scaffolds, where predictions far from the mean tend to be the most wrong under a MAE loss. Set s as a module-level constant so it is easy to change.

title: Yeo-Johnson power transform for SVR inputs instead of quantile normal
spec: In the SVR branch, replace the QuantileTransformer with sklearn.preprocessing.PowerTransformer(method='yeo-johnson', standardize=True) fitted on the kept descriptor columns of the training set (keep = Xtr.std(axis=0) > 0 as now). Apply transform to the test set. Before the transform, clip each descriptor column to the 1st and 99th percentiles of the training data to tame extreme values. Leave the LightGBM member, the SVR hyperparameters (C=3, epsilon=0.1, gamma='scale') and the 50/50 blend unchanged. Wrap the transform in a try/except that falls back to the existing quantile transform if the power fit fails to converge.

title: Morgan fingerprints with chirality and ring-membership invariants for the tree member
spec: Replace the Morgan generator with rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganGenerator(radius=2, fpSize=1024, includeChirality=True) and compute count fingerprints with GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy. Add ring-membership information by building a second generator with atomInvariantsGenerator from rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganFeatureAtomInvGen() only for radius 1, appended as 256 bits. Concatenate these count features to the existing RDKit descriptors for the LightGBM member only. The SVR member keeps the descriptors only, as now. Keep all hyperparameters and the 50/50 blend unchanged.

title: Physchem linear baseline with LightGBM on its residuals
spec: Inside fit_predict, first fit a Ridge regression (alpha=10) on the quantile-normalized, kept descriptor matrix (use the same QuantileTransformer as the SVR branch) to predict y, using only the training data. Compute residuals r = y - ridge_prediction on the training set, and train the LightGBM member (unchanged hyperparameters) on r instead of y. The final LightGBM prediction is ridge_test_prediction + lgb_residual_prediction. Keep the SVR member on y and the 50/50 blend unchanged. The linear baseline captures the global trend in polarity and size, and the trees model the remaining nonlinear structure.

title: MACCS+FCFP counts for LightGBM only
spec: Keep the SVR on the quantile-normalized RDKit descriptors only. Build extra features for LightGBM only: 167 MACCS keys (rdkit.Chem.MACCSkeys.GenMACCSKeys, as 0/1 array) and a 512-bit feature-invariant Morgan count fingerprint (radius 2, rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganGenerator with atomInvariantsGenerator=GetMorganFeatureAtomInvGen(), GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy). Concatenate them to the descriptor matrix for the LightGBM fit and predict, and leave the SVR input unchanged. Keep the 50/50 blend.

title: Salt stripping and largest fragment
spec: In featurize, parse each SMILES, keep only the largest fragment by heavy atom count (rdkit.Chem.rdmolops.GetMolFrags with asMols=True, then max by GetNumHeavyAtoms) before computing descriptors. Leave everything else unchanged.

title: kNN third blend member
spec: Add a KNeighborsRegressor (k=7, weights='distance', metric euclidean) fitted on the quantile-normalized descriptors Str already computed for the SVR. Blend as 0.4 LightGBM + 0.4 SVR + 0.2 kNN.

title: SVR on LightGBM residuals
spec: Fit LightGBM first. Get out-of-fold LightGBM predictions on the training set with 5-fold KFold (seeded). Fit the RBF SVR (C=3, eps=0.1) on the quantile-normalized descriptors to predict the OOF residual y minus oof. The final prediction is the LightGBM full-fit prediction plus 0.7 times the SVR residual prediction on the test set.

title: Rank-normal target transform for SVR
spec: For the SVR member only, fit on a transformed target: standardize y to z-scores, then map to ranks and to normal quantiles (scipy.stats.norm.ppf((rank-0.5)/n)). Map SVR predictions back by interpolating on the sorted training y values (np.interp over the sorted normal quantiles). LightGBM stays on the raw target. Keep the 50/50 blend.

title: SVR feature-subset bagging
spec: Replace the single SVR with an average of 8 SVRs (C=3, eps=0.1). Each is trained on a random 60% subset of the quantile-normalized descriptor columns, drawn with np.random.RandomState(seed+i). Average their predictions and use that as the SVR side of the 50/50 blend.

title: Gaussian-noise augmentation for SVR
spec: For the SVR only, stack the quantile-normalized training matrix Str with 2 noisy copies (add N(0,0.15) noise with a seeded RNG) and replicate y accordingly. Fit the SVR (C=3, eps=0.1) on the augmented set. Keep LightGBM and the 50/50 blend unchanged.

title: LightGBM DART
spec: Change the LightGBM member to boosting_type='dart' with n_estimators=400, learning_rate=0.06, drop_rate=0.1, skip_drop=0.5, and the other parameters as they are. Keep the SVR and the 50/50 blend.

title: Inner importance-based feature selection
spec: Fit LightGBM once on all descriptors. Keep the top 120 features by gain importance (booster_.feature_importance('gain')). Refit LightGBM on those columns only. Use the same subset for the SVR after the quantile transform, applying the keep mask. Keep the 50/50 blend.

title: Blend weight 0.4/0.6 toward SVR
spec: Change the final blend to 0.4 times the LightGBM prediction plus 0.6 times the SVR prediction. Change nothing else.

title: MACCS + FCFP counts for LightGBM only
spec: The closest candidate so far (0.3599/0.3615) appended 167 MACCS keys and 512-bit feature-Morgan counts to the descriptors for both blend members. Repeat that feature addition but give the extra bits to LightGBM only, leaving the SVR on the quantile-normalized RDKit descriptors exactly as it is today. Concretely: build the descriptor matrix as now; additionally compute MACCSkeys.GenMACCSKeys (167 bits, as float) and a 512-bit radius-2 feature-invariant Morgan count fingerprint (rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganGenerator(radius=2, fpSize=512, atomInvariantsGenerator=GetMorganFeatureAtomInvGen()), GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy) per molecule, concatenate descriptors+MACCS+FCFP for the LightGBM fit/predict, and keep the SVR branch on the descriptor block alone. Keep the 50/50 average and all LightGBM hyperparameters unchanged. Cache featurization so each SMILES is parsed once.

title: Salt stripping and largest-fragment canonicalization
spec: Clean each SMILES before featurization so that counterions and solvates do not distort the descriptors. In featurize, after Chem.MolFromSmiles, keep only the largest fragment by heavy-atom count (Chem.GetMolFrags(m, asMols=True) and pick the max, falling back to the whole molecule if fragmentation fails), then neutralize nothing else and recompute all descriptors on that fragment. If the molecule fails to parse, fall back to a zero row as now. Everything else (LightGBM settings, quantile transform, SVR, 50/50 blend) stays identical. This is a pure input-cleaning change and should cost no extra runtime.

title: Rank-normal target transform for the SVR member
spec: The SVR sees a skewed target; map it to a Gaussian before fitting. Inside fit_predict, fit a QuantileTransformer(output_distribution='normal', n_quantiles=min(200, len(y)), random_state=seed) on train_y reshaped to (-1,1), fit the RBF SVR (same C=3, epsilon=0.1, gamma='scale') on the transformed target, then invert the transform on the SVR test predictions with inverse_transform before blending. LightGBM keeps the raw target. Keep the 50/50 average and the existing descriptor quantile scaling of the features unchanged.

title: kNN as a third blend member
spec: Add a distance-weighted k-nearest-neighbour regressor as a cheap, low-bias third member. Reuse the quantile-normal-scaled descriptor matrix that already feeds the SVR (Str/Ste) and fit KNeighborsRegressor(n_neighbors=10, weights='distance', metric='euclidean', n_jobs=8) on it. Blend the three predictions with fixed weights 0.45 LightGBM, 0.45 SVR, 0.10 kNN. Nothing else changes; the kNN adds negligible runtime.

title: Shift the blend weight toward the SVR
spec: The two members are currently averaged 50/50 with no evidence that this is the optimum, and the pure-SVR run (0.3849) was much worse than pure LightGBM-ish baselines, so the optimum may sit slightly off centre. Change the final line to 0.4 * p_lgb + 0.6 * svr.predict(Ste). Change nothing else. This is a one-number edit; it settles the direction of the weight so later ideas need not guess.

title: Feature-subset bagging for the SVR
spec: Replace the single RBF SVR with an average of 5 SVRs, each trained on a random 60% subset of the kept (non-constant) descriptor columns, drawn with np.random.default_rng(seed). Fit the QuantileTransformer once on all kept columns as now, then index the scaled matrices by each column subset; each SVR keeps kernel='rbf', C=3, epsilon=0.1, gamma='scale'. Average the 5 test predictions into a single svr prediction and keep the 50/50 blend with LightGBM. This decorrelates the kernel member at roughly 5x the SVR cost, which is small relative to the 10-minute budget.

title: Residual stacking: SVR on LightGBM out-of-fold residuals
spec: Instead of averaging the two members, let the SVR model what LightGBM gets wrong. Build 5-fold out-of-fold LightGBM predictions on the training set (KFold(5, shuffle=True, random_state=seed), same LightGBM settings), form residuals r = y - oof_pred, fit the RBF SVR (C=3, epsilon=0.1, gamma='scale') on the quantile-normal-scaled descriptors with target r, refit LightGBM on all training data, and predict p_lgb + svr.predict(Ste) for the test molecules. Shrink the correction by a factor 0.7 to guard against overfitting the residuals. Runtime is about 6 LightGBM fits per fold, which fits the budget.

title: Inner-CV feature selection by LightGBM importance
spec: The ~210 RDKit descriptors include many near-useless columns that hurt the kernel member in particular. Fit one quick LightGBM (same hyperparameters, 200 trees) on the full training descriptors, rank columns by gain importance, and keep the top 80 columns. Re-fit the main LightGBM on those 80 columns and also restrict the SVR's quantile-scaled input to those same columns (intersected with the non-constant mask). Keep the 50/50 blend and everything else unchanged. Use random_state=seed for the selector fit so the selection is deterministic per fold.

title: Add truncated-SVD components of atom-pair counts
spec: Compress a structural fingerprint into a few dense columns so both members can use it without blowing up dimensionality. Compute 2048-bit hashed atom-pair count fingerprints (rdFingerprintGenerator.GetAtomPairGenerator(fpSize=2048), GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy), apply log1p, fit TruncatedSVD(n_components=32, random_state=seed) on the training fingerprints only, transform train and test, and append the 32 components to the RDKit descriptor matrix used by both LightGBM and the SVR (the SVR's quantile transform then covers the appended columns too). Keep the 50/50 blend and all model hyperparameters unchanged.

title: Gaussian-noise augmentation for the SVR
spec: Regularize the kernel member by training it on a noise-augmented copy of the data. After the quantile-normal scaling of the descriptors, build an augmented training set of 3 copies: the original Str plus 2 copies with independent Gaussian noise of sd 0.1 added to every feature, drawn with np.random.default_rng(seed), with the target tiled unchanged. Fit the same RBF SVR (C=3, epsilon=0.1, gamma='scale') on the ~2200-row augmented matrix and predict on the clean Ste. LightGBM and the 50/50 blend are untouched. The SVR cost grows roughly 9x but stays small.

title: MACCS + FCFP counts for LightGBM only, SVR unchanged
spec: Build a second feature block: 167 MACCS keys (rdkit.Chem.MACCSkeys.GenMACCSKeys) and 512-bit radius-2 feature-invariant Morgan count fingerprints (rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganGenerator(radius=2, fpSize=512, atomInvariantsGenerator=rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganFeatureAtomInvGen()), GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy). Concatenate this block to the RDKit descriptors only for the LightGBM input. The SVR keeps the current input exactly: quantile-normalized RDKit descriptors only. Keep the 50/50 blend and all hyperparameters. Compute molecules once per SMILES and reuse them for both blocks.

title: Charge-state and ionization features at pH 7.4
spec: Append a small block of ionization features to the descriptor matrix (used by both LightGBM and the SVR): SMARTS-match counts for carboxylic acids, tetrazoles, acyl sulfonamides, phosphates/sulfonates (acidic groups); primary, secondary, tertiary aliphatic amines not adjacent to carbonyl, amidines, guanidines (basic groups); quaternary nitrogen. Derive from them: number of acidic groups, number of basic groups, estimated net charge (basic minus acidic), a zwitterion flag (both > 0), and a neutral flag. Also add TPSA/MolWt, HBD count / heavy atom count, and MolLogP - TPSA/50. Keep everything else unchanged.

title: Largest-fragment and neutralization standardization before featurizing
spec: In featurize, standardize each molecule before computing descriptors: use rdkit.Chem.MolStandardize.rdMolStandardize to keep the largest fragment (LargestFragmentChooser) and then neutralize charges (Uncharger). If standardization fails, fall back to the original molecule. Silence RDKit logging with RDLogger.DisableLog('rdApp.*'). Compute all descriptors on the standardized molecule. Model, blend and hyperparameters stay the same.

title: kNN regressor as a third blend member
spec: Add a KNeighborsRegressor (n_neighbors=7, weights='distance', Euclidean metric) fitted on the same quantile-normalized, constant-column-filtered descriptor matrix Str that the SVR uses. Predict on Ste. Change the final blend to 0.45 * LightGBM + 0.45 * SVR + 0.10 * kNN. Nothing else changes.

title: SVR on LightGBM out-of-fold residuals
spec: Replace the parallel 50/50 blend with residual stacking. Get 5-fold out-of-fold LightGBM predictions on the training set (KFold with shuffle=True, random_state=seed, same LightGBM settings). Compute residuals y - oof. Fit the RBF SVR (C=3, epsilon=0.05, gamma='scale') on the quantile-normalized descriptors to predict these residuals. Fit the LightGBM on the full training set for the test prediction. Final prediction = LightGBM(test) + 0.7 * SVR_residual(test).

title: Feature-subset bagging of the SVR
spec: Replace the single SVR with a bag of 15 SVRs. For each bag member i, draw a random 60% subset of the kept quantile-normalized descriptor columns with np.random.default_rng(seed + i), fit SVR(kernel='rbf', C=3, epsilon=0.1, gamma='scale') on those columns, and predict the test rows. Average the 15 predictions to form the SVR member. Keep the LightGBM member and the 50/50 blend unchanged.

title: Top-importance feature selection for the SVR
spec: After fitting the LightGBM on the training descriptors, take its gain-based feature importances (model.booster_.feature_importance(importance_type='gain')). Keep only the 80 descriptors with the highest gain (among non-constant columns) as the SVR input, then quantile-normalize these and fit the same SVR (C=3, epsilon=0.1, gamma='scale'). The selection uses training data only, inside fit_predict. LightGBM keeps all descriptors; the blend stays 50/50.

title: LightGBM with DART boosting
spec: Change the LightGBM blend member to DART: boosting_type='dart', drop_rate=0.1, skip_drop=0.5, max_drop=50, n_estimators=600, learning_rate=0.05, and keep num_leaves=15, subsample=0.8, subsample_freq=1, colsample_bytree=0.5, min_child_samples=10, random_state=seed, n_jobs=8, verbose=-1. The SVR member and the 50/50 blend stay the same.

title: Slower, longer LightGBM with feature sampling per node
spec: Change only the LightGBM hyperparameters: n_estimators=1500, learning_rate=0.01, num_leaves=15, max_depth=6, subsample=0.7, subsample_freq=1, colsample_bytree=0.5, feature_fraction_bynode=0.5, min_child_samples=8, random_state=seed, n_jobs=8, verbose=-1. The SVR member and the 50/50 blend stay the same.

title: Linear-tree LightGBM as a third blend member on a compact physchem set
spec: Add a third member: LGBMRegressor(linear_tree=True, linear_lambda=1.0, n_estimators=300, learning_rate=0.03, num_leaves=4, min_child_samples=30, subsample=0.8, subsample_freq=1, colsample_bytree=0.8, random_state=seed, n_jobs=8, verbose=-1) trained on a compact slice of the descriptor matrix: the columns of Descriptors.descList named MolLogP, MolMR, TPSA, MolWt, NumHDonors, NumHAcceptors, NumRotatableBonds, FractionCSP3, HeavyAtomCount, RingCount, NumAromaticRings, LabuteASA, BalabanJ, BertzCT, qed, MaxPartialCharge, MinPartialCharge. Select the columns by name from descList. Final blend: 0.4 * LightGBM + 0.4 * SVR + 0.2 * linear-tree model.
